Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on April 19, 2019
Review Body:
I picked up the book because I’m interested in the subject of “Tyranny”, and because this book had such a powerful two word title: “On Tyranny”. I immediately thought, this must be a classic on the level of “Atlas Shrugged” – or “The Prince”, “The Metamorphosis”, or “The Odyssey”.

It is a compendium of patently obvious truisms, supported by some good historical accounts of tyrannical malfeasance by regimes from all political ends of the spectrum. The author must know something about this subject.

Such a magnanimous attempt to impress on the audience the dangers of tyrannical regimes, past and present, should certainly be a transparent and objective endeavor in an attempt to discover the truth of tyranny.

It began in an innocuous fashion, each chapter factually supporting a stated truism with some good historical context. But after several chapters, planted at the end of a certain chapter was an insidious reference to a political rally with chants of “USA”, USA, and mention of security guards escorting protesters. The author further digs in later on to showcase other forms of “tyrannical” behavior exemplified by the current USA political administration – the President calling people names, like" Lyin’ Ted”. Also is mention of numerous false statements made in public by the current administration.

All of this targeted at the current political administration in the USA. But never was a mention made of the lies, deceptions of past administrations (including the prior administration, and the administration before it – some quite deceptive and harmful to our society (ie., the cost of lives). None of this to balance the thesis of the author.

Does this author not know that tyranny is not left, or right, or in the middle of the political spectrum? Tyranny is tyranny, regardless of political proclivity. Does the author not know that tyrannical behavior has occurred many times during the 20th century? If so, then why does he not balance the essay with other examples on all ends of the political spectrum?

I read an Op Ed in a famous Wall Street publication today in which the author said, the President is not guilty of destroying Democracy, he is guilty of destroying political etiquette. And then I thought about this book. This author must be so blinded with such contempt that he can’t see the difference between licentious behavior of the individual he targets and the true tyranny ongoing in our ruling political class of today.

The author even goes so far as to recommend that the audience watch less TV and read more books, in order to (I presume) be more clairvoyant. I totally concur, but I would not recommend this book as a read , as it is no more objective than the trash we see on 24 hour TV today.

There is one quality of this piece of work that I would rate highly --- it’s brevity. It permitted me to dispose of it rapidly. I venture to say this book must have been written over a weekend while the author sailed in New Haven Harbor.
